correctness.rationale: With conserved opposite currents J and −J, the two stationary densities are uniquely fixed up to J by the wall values J/κ, and reflection exchanges them. For example ρ_+(x)=J/v+(J/κ−J/v)e^(p(x/L−1)), nonnegative for J>0 as a convex combination of the two endpoint coefficients. Normalization fixes J and yields c=p/(p+β−1+e^−p); the denominator is positive. The centered cosh density has second moment 1/4+2/p²−coth(p/2)/p. Its strict positive excess over 1/12 follows by strict positive covariance of y² with the cosh weight under the uniform law. Thus the sign is that of β−1+e^−p. The objective tends to 1/12 at p→0 and p→∞; when 0<β<1 the positive gain after H guarantees an interior global optimum. For δ→0, the test p=H+log H gives gain ∼δ/(6H), while p≥(1+ε)H has gain bounded by δ/[6((1+ε)H−δ)]; hence every optimum has p/H→1. Writing u=e^−p, log differentiation of the gain gives u/(δ−u)=(1−u)/(p−δ+u)−B′/B, with B′/B=6/p²+O(p^−3). Converting the resulting 1/p−6/p² to u/δ contributes one more unit, giving 1/p−7/p²+O(p^−3). Taking logarithms and expanding about H gives the stated optimizer; the gain at that point is δ/(6p)(1−7/p+O(p^−2)), yielding the stated depth. No uniqueness of the optimizer is used.
residual_risks: The checker is bounded and supplementary. The signed coefficient 1−c can be negative (the formula is not always a probabilistic convex mixture), but the current representation ensures nonnegative densities. The normalization of the wall reaction and of the variance is essential.

value.rationale: Even with an exact stationary variance, the weak-confinement design problem near threshold has a diverging optimizer and a shrinking depth. The log-log scale separates the optimum from the sign-change point, and the paired location and depth coefficients quantify the singular balance under a natural fixed-rates length variation. This adds more than rewriting the known variance.
residual_risks: Specific wall normalization and normalized variance; the result does not optimize Var(X) itself or establish uniqueness at finite β.
